claim: For binary fix-free codes whose codeword lengths lie in \(\{2,3,4\}\), let \(a_j\) be the number of codewords of length \(j\), and for each feasible pair \((a_2,a_3)\) let \(M(a_2,a_3)\) be the largest possible \(a_4\). The complete table is \(M(0,\cdot)=(16,13,10,8,6,4,2,1,0)\) for \(a_3=0,\ldots,8\), \(M(1,\cdot)=(9,7,6,5,4,1)\) for \(a_3=0,\ldots,5\), \(M(2,\cdot)=(4,3,2)\) for \(a_3=0,1,2\), \(M(3,\cdot)=(1,0)\) for \(a_3=0,1\), and \(M(4,0)=0\); all other \((a_2,a_3)\) pairs are infeasible. Hence \((a_2,a_3,a_4)\) is realizable exactly when its pair is listed and \(0\le a_4\le M(a_2,a_3)\). In particular, every profile of Kraft sum at most \(3/4\) is realizable, while the first impossible discrete Kraft level above \(3/4\) is \(13/16\), where the unique impossible profile is \((2,0,5)\).
integrity: The complete finite reduction was reconstructed from the definition, and the bundled verifier exhausts all 4096 shorter-layer selections and the full profile grid through Kraft sum \(1\). The verifier was replayed directly from the embedded verification artifact before release.
scientific_limitations: The classification is specific to binary fix-free codes supported on lengths \(2,3,4\). It neither characterizes arbitrary length multisets nor claims a general improvement to the \(3/4\) theorem. Bibliographic residual risk remains for an unindexed historical small-profile enumeration.
title: Exact profile boundary for binary fix-free codes on lengths \(2,3,4\)
